source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A finding entirely unrelated to diabetes risk, contrary to why this particular postprandial test was actually ordered for this client","B":"Hypoglycemia requiring immediate carbohydrate intake, which is the opposite of what this elevated reading actually indicates","C":"Impaired glucose tolerance, warranting further evaluation, rather than the meaningless post-meal blip the client is currently assuming this represents","D":"Normal glucose metabolism requiring no further testing, contrary to what this significantly elevated result actually warrants"}}
source_row.rationale: An elevated 2-hour postprandial blood glucose level suggests impaired glucose tolerance, which may indicate prediabetes or diabetes, warranting further evaluation (such as additional testing, including a formal oral glucose tolerance test or HbA1c) to confirm the diagnosis and guide management.
source_row.source_name: American Diabetes Association — Postprandial Glucose Testing Interpretation
source_row.stem: A client's 2-hour postprandial blood glucose comes back significantly elevated, and the client assumes this single reading couldn't really mean much since it was taken right after a big meal. The nurse should recognize this finding as suggestive of:
